Article Title: PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, offers condolences over mother's death
Article Text:
PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, condoles death of his mother

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and expressed condolences over the death of his mother, Savitri Devi , who passed away at the age of 91 in her native village in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district.Savitri Devi died around 10.45 am on Friday in Panchur village, residents told PTI. She had been unwell for a long time and could recognise only family members, a member of the Panchur Gram Sabha said.Pauri Garhwal Senior Superintendent of Police Sarvesh Panwar said the local administration was in touch with the family.Adityanath was attending a public function in Uttar Pradesh when he received the news of his mother's death. He had two more official engagements scheduled for later in the day and was expected to continue with his programme. It was not immediately clear whether he would travel to Uttarakhand for the last rites, which are likely to be held on Saturday.G C Badola, a member of the Panchur Gram Sabha, told PTI, “One of her sons is posted in Kotdwar and will reach the village by Friday evening. The last rites will likely be conducted at Phool Chatti Ghat near the village on Saturday, where the last rites of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s father were also held.”Defence minister Rajnath Singh expressed grief over Savitri Devi's death in a post on X, saying the loss of a mother was one of the most unbearable blows in life. He extended his condolences to Adityanath and his family.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also described her death as extremely sad and heartbreaking, saying, "Her demise is an irreparable loss to the family." He extended his condolences to the bereaved family and prayed for strength for them to cope with the loss.Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, along with state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, also condoled her death and prayed for peace for the departed soul and strength for the family.Adityanath's father, Anand Singh Bisht, died following a prolonged illness in 2020. His last rites were performed in Uttarakhand. Adityanath did not attend the funeral due to the Covid-19 lockdown and his responsibilities as Uttar Pradesh chief minister.
Article Summary: PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, condoles death of his mother Savitri Devi. She died at the age of 91 in her native village in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district. Last rites will likely be conducted at Phool Chatti Ghat near the village on Saturday.

Article Title: Pakistan analyst claims no Indian official welcomed Musadik Malik in Delhi; fact-checked
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A claim by Pakistani think tank analyst that no Indian official was present to receive Pakistan's minister Musadik Masood Malik, upon his arrival in New Delhi has been contradicted by official sources cited by news agency ANI.Khurram Abbas alleged that India had not extended the customary official welcome to Malik, who arrived in the national capital on Thursday to attend the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum."India didn’t show courtesy to send official to welcome Pakistan climate change and environmental coordination minister Musadik Malik who arrived in Delhi to attend SCO meeting. He was welcomed by the Pakistani CdA. First Pakistan minister in India since 2023 & May 2025 conflict," Abbas alleged in a post on X.However, according to sources cited by news agency ANI, a director from the Union ministry of culture and an under secretary from the Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division of the MEA were present at the airport to receive Malik as part of the welcome protocol.The sources also clarified that all SCO member countries arriving in New Delhi were being extended a similar level of protocol.Malik's visit is significant as he is the first Pakistani minister to travel to India in three years and the first since the May 2025 military confrontation between the two nuclear-armed countries following the Pahalgam terror attack , in which 26 people were killed by Pakistan-backed terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir The last high-profile visit by a Pakistani political leader was that of then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari in 2023.Malik is in New Delhi to participate in the thematic sessions of the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, scheduled to be held from November 20 to 22.According to Pakistan's ministry of foreign affairs, Malik will represent Islamabad at the forum and present Pakistan's perspective on the importance of dialogue among civilisations and its role in diplomacy.In a statement, the ministry said the minister's address would highlight Pakistan's constructive role in the SCO, along with the country's diverse civilisational and cultural heritage."Pakistan's participation in this Forum is reflective of its contribution as an active State to promote dialogue, cooperation and understanding in line with the 'Shanghai Spirit'," the statement said.Pakistan's participation follows India's invitation to all 10 SCO member states, along with observer countries and dialogue partners, to attend the inaugural forum.The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had earlier confirmed that several countries, including SCO member states, had been invited to the event, adding that New Delhi looked forward to hosting the dialogue.Proposed by India, the initiative aims to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding and people-to-people ties across the Eurasian region.Defence minister Rajnath Singh had announced India's plan to host the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20.The SCO has 10 member states, including India, Pakistan, China and Russia. India became a full member of the grouping in 2017.
Article Summary: Pakistan's climate change and environmental coordination minister Musadik Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi on Thursday. Malik is in India to attend the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum. Think tank analyst Khurram Abbas alleged that India had not extended the customary official welcome to Malik. But sources cited by news agency ANI said an under secretary from the Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division of the MEA was present at the airport.

Odisha has stepped up preparations as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast, with nearly 3 lakh people evacuated, hundreds of rescue personnel deployed and thousands of shelters readied.The IMD has forecast that the storm is likely to make landfall between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon, with wind speeds of 90-100 kmph.2,98,676 people had been evacuated to safer locations across Odisha by Thursday evening, PTI reported, quoting Sspecial relief commissioner(SRC) Rajesh P Patil. The state has set up 2,523 relief camps and prepared 9,341 cyclone shelters.A total of 423 rescue teams have been deployed in vulnerable areas. These include 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams, 14 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 131 Fire and Emergency Services teams. The Coast Guard has also been asked to keep helicopters, vessels and other logistical support ready.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that Cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the Odisha coast between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon or afternoon.IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the system was expected to cross as a cyclonic storm, with wind speeds of 90-100 kmph. Winds of 70-80 kmph are likely along parts of the Odisha coast, with the system expected to weaken as it moves northwards.The cyclone was around 410 km from Gopalpur and 470 km from Puri on Thursday evening, moving at a speed of 13 kmph, according to an IMD official.Odisha chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi chaired an emergency midnight review meeting at the Special Relief Commissioner's (SRC) office in Bhubaneswar to take stock of the state's final preparations for Cyclone Akvan."Today, I reviewed the preparations for the cyclone. According to information received from the IMD, the cyclone is now expected to make landfall along the Odisha coast... The situation has now become clearer. Based on this, we have intensified our preparations across 20 districts," Majhi said.He said evacuation to safer locations was progressing rapidly following earlier reviews and discussions with district magistrates of the 20 districts.Of the 9,341 cyclone shelters prepared across the state, 2,623 are currently operational, the chief minister said.The state has also identified 941 landslide-prone locations across six districts, primarily in hilly areas. "All teams are fully prepared to handle any eventuality," Majhi said.These include Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput and Malkangiri, with Gajapati accounting for 211 locations.Rail services have been disrupted as a precaution. East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29, while the South Eastern Railway cancelled 28 express trains, mostly those operating to and from Puri.Tourists have been barred from visiting Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika. Schools have also been closed in districts under red, orange and yellow weather alerts.The Gundicha Temple in Puri will remain closed from November 19 to 21, while the Jagannath Temple will remain open. Nandankanan Zoological Park and Botanical Garden have been closed on November 19 and 20. Bhitarkanika National Park will remain shut until November 21, and Similipal National Park on November 20 and 21.Neighbouring Andhra Pradesh has also stepped up preparedness. The IMD has issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, an orange alert for Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli, and a yellow alert for Kakinada.At Paradip Port, six fishing boats carrying 54 fishermen have been provided safe harbour, ANI reported. In Balasore, the district administration has identified 145 permanent cyclone shelters and 1,250 temporary shelters. District magistrate Suryawanshi Mayur Vikas said teams were ready to relocate 12,000-15,000 people, with a contingency plan to evacuate up to 2.5 lakh if required.The IMD has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in parts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely in Visakhapatnam and adjoining districts. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea until the morning of November 21.Nearly a month after the monsoon withdrew in mid-October, Tripura is bracing for scattered rain and isolated thunderstorms as Cyclone Akvan's outer cloud bands draw moisture into the Northeast.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated thunderstorms and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph across the state on Thursday and Friday, with some areas likely to see thunderstorm activity on November 22. A yellow alert has been issued for South Tripura, Gomati and Sepahijala for Thursday.Isolated heavy rainfall is also expected in West Tripura, Sepahijala, Gomati and South Tripura on Friday and Saturday. The IMD has ruled out any threat of a direct cyclone strike or severe winds in the state.Akvan is moving towards the Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh coasts and remains far from Tripura. Its indirect influence is expected to keep weather conditions unsettled for the next few days. Temperatures are likely to remain near normal, with foggy conditions possibly setting in next week and a sharper winter chill expected in early December.Read More: Cyclone Akvan Live Updates
Article Summary: Odisha has stepped up preparations as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast. Nearly 3 lakh people evacuated, hundreds of rescue personnel deployed and thousands of shelters readied. Storm is likely to make landfall between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi slammed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's foreign policy saying "India has become a side player" in global affairs, while citing Pakistan's role in facilitating peace talks between the US and Iran.Speaking at an interaction with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (local time), Rahul said, "India, by its size, naturally has a global voice and India should be actively involved in global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player.""I'm pretty shocked that Pakistan is busy negotiating with the Iranians and the Americans, and India's just looking," he added.The Lok Sabha leader of opposition said that India had played a prominent role in global affairs after Independence, particularly through the Non-Aligned Movement and expressed a desire to see New Delhi regain that stature.Rahul also questioned PM Modi's reliance on personal relationships with world leaders, including US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, arguing that diplomatic and geopolitical decisions could not be driven by individual equations."Friendship is not the point. Who gives a damn about friendship? Do you really think that geopolitics is going to work because the guy is your friend? He's leading a structure.He's got a whole economic system under him," Rahul said during the interaction, moderated by Professor Robert Pape."He's not going to make decisions based on whether he likes you or doesn't like you. So these are some of the things that disturb me,” he added.He clarified that he had no objection to leaders maintaining personal friendships, but said foreign policy should be guided by a clear understanding of national interests and India's position in the world."I don't have a problem with being friends with Mr Modi or being friends with leaders. Friendship is not that important. What's important is that you understand what's going on, who you are, and where you fit," he said."The next global architecture will not be built by one civilisation alone. It will be shaped by multiple civilisations, with America, China, India, the Middle East and Russia all having a role to play," he added.The remarks come amid renewed tensions in the Gulf, with diplomatic efforts to ease the US-Iran conflict facing setbacks. The earlier ceasefire and diplomatic framework have broken down, while negotiations remain stalled over differences on sanctions, the US naval blockade and the Strait of Hormuz.Responding to a question from a Pakistani participant on the possibility of improving bilateral ties, Rahul Gandhi said dialogue with Islamabad could begin if Pakistan stopped supporting and encouraging terrorism in India.Rahul said India could not engage in talks while innocent people continued to be killed in terror attacks allegedly backed by Pakistan."The moment that stops, a conversation can potentially begin," he said, adding that accepting such violence while maintaining dialogue was impossible for India.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi's foreign policy saying "India has become a side player" in global affairs. He cites Pakistan's role in facilitating peace talks between the US and Iran. The remarks come amid renewed tensions in the Gulf with diplomatic efforts to ease the US-Iran conflict facing setbacks.

Article Title: 3 leopards found dead in North Kashmir, poisoning suspected
Article Text:
Three leopard cubs were found dead within two days in Tangmarg area of Jammu and Kashmir’s Baramulla district

SRINAGAR: Three leopards, including two female cubs aged 8-9 months, were found dead in the forests of north Kashmir’s Kunzar area, prompting J&K’s wildlife protection department to file an FIR Thursday against unknown people after autopsies raised suspicion of poisoning.Wildlife official Shahid Sultan said the cubs were found dead on Nov 17, with no visible injury marks. Their bodies were kept overnight at the department’s control room in Tangmarg because a veterinarian was unavailable. Autopsies were conducted the next day. On Wednesday, police informed the department about another dead leopard, an 8-9-year-old male. All three were found in the same area, though not together, Sultan said.“The doctors in their reports have mentioned a suspected case of poisoning,” he said, adding they had also raised the possibility of infectious poisoning, suspecting the animals might have eaten contaminated meat, possibly a rabid dog. Samples were collected for forensic examination to establish the cause of death. “We have not come across such a case of suspected poisoning before,” he said.Leopard sightings are common, particularly in north Kashmir, where mountainous terrain and expanding apple orchards provide suitable habitat. On Nov 10, six-year-old boy Kifayat Bhat was mauled to death by a leopard in Kreeri.
Article Summary: Three leopards, including two female cubs aged 8-9 months, were found dead in the forests of north Kashmir’s Kunzar area. Autopsies raised suspicion of poisoning, suspecting the animals might have eaten contaminated meat, possibly a rabid dog.

NEW DELHI: Amid recent attacks on commercial vessels with Indian crew members in the Persian Gulf, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Thursday directed the country’s maritime regulator to step up surveillance of high-risk areas, issue timely security advisories and sensitise seafarers about potential threats and precautionary measures.Between Nov 10 and 18, at least five reported incidents involving commercial vessels carrying Indian seafarers occurred in the Persian Gulf and around the Strait of Hormuz. The attacks involved projectiles and missiles, leaving Indian crew members injured, one missing and vessels damaged or evacuated.Chairing a review meeting on Thursday, Sonowal also directed the directorate general of maritime administration (DGMA) to maintain regular communication with shipping companies and vessel operators to ensure the safety of Indian seafarers. He asked officials to coordinate closely with the ministry of external affairs, Indian diplomatic missions, maritime stakeholders and international agencies to ensure prompt assistance in the event of an incident involving Indian vessels or seafarers.Currently, nine Indian-flagged or Indian-interest vessels carrying 161 Indian seafarers are in the Persian Gulf. In the Red Sea, eight Indian-flagged vessels have 210 Indian seafarers on board.The ministry is tracking more than 1,200 vessels and nearly 9,500 Indian seafarers in high-risk regions through a live dashboard launched for this purpose.So far, 104 incidents have been reported in the Persian Gulf, claiming 12 Indian lives. Another 37 incidents have been reported in the Black Sea, where five Indian seafarers have lost their lives.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has ruled out bilateral talks with Pakistan until Islamabad stops supporting cross-border terrorism, saying India cannot engage in dialogue while its citizens continue to be killed in terror attacks.Speaking at the University of Chicago in Illinois on Wednesday, Gandhi was asked whether India and Pakistan could move beyond mutual accusations and explore cooperation. Article Title: Shenzhen Trilateral: India cautious amid possible vindication and strategic concerns
Article Text:
Shenzhen Trilateral: India cautious amid possible vindication and strategic concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Shenzhen trilateral summit may not signal a crisis for India but the government is closely following the likely outcomes, realising the meeting's potential to alter several dynamics that it has to manage almost on a daily basis in its ties with the US, China and Russia.There was no official response from India to the "historic" 90-minute meeting that President Donald Trump had with his Chinese and Russian counterparts – Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin respectively – in China's global tech hub but official sources said India is following the summit and likely ramifications with strategic caution.The meeting, which was described as positive and highly productive by the Chinese state media, ended with a declaration that committed to UN reforms, to deal more effectively with global challenges, stable energy flows, nuclear risk reduction and the "abuse" of its jurisdiction by the International Criminal Court (ICC) that issued an arrest warrant against Putin. India is not a party to the ICC and mainatins safe distance from it.Overhauling the UN – with focus on expanding the Security Council permanent membership - and securing stable and predictable energy supplies have been core pillars of India's foreign policy in a world marred by conflicts. Any indication of urgency for UN reforms is a positive development. However, there's also little for India to believe that the call for the UN to conform to its "fundamental mission" of peace and security is more than just lip service.India holds P5 countries responsible for the delay in Security Council reforms and external affairs minister S Jaishankar has accused these countries of being "short-sighted" by not agreeing to any dilution of their powers.The focus on stable energy flows does provide some diplomatic vindication for its long-standing position that Russian oil purchase helped stabilize global energy markets. It's also important that the declaration talks about expanding the production and supply of refined petroleum products, as India emerges as a crucial processing hub, refining Russian crude. For India, any potential easing of the rigid US position on India's energy policy would be a welcome development.The statement that in the declaration shunning nuclear war also aligns with India's core nuclear doctrine. India had welcomed the same formulation in a P5 2022 joint statement, saying that it creates a security environment conducive to global disarmament.Looking ahead, there are concerns that India might have about the likely implications from the meeting, and the answers to which might lie in doubling down on its strategic autonomy and multi alignment. Despite its time-tested ties with Russia, a great power cartel or a G3 that operates as an exclusive club to manage global affairs may not sit easily with India's focus on a multipolar world and multipolar Asia or its efforts to lead the Global South into a decision-making role.There was no direct mention of the wars in West Asia and Ukraine where India is keen to support early resolution and has even put forward a proposal for safety of commercial shipping, while working to secure shipping lanes also in the Strait of Hormuz. India has argued that the Global South cannot remain a helpless spectator and must have a role in shaping peaceful settlements of conflicts that have most impacted the developing world.While much has been made about the US signalling to China through the Manila Quad summit, India realizes it must remain vigilant against the consequences of a US-China accommodation. Any understanding between Washington and Beijing that upsets the Indo-Pacific balance may not be in India's interest. Even the Quad summit took place after 2 years and only on the margins of a multilateral event.
Article Summary: No official response from India to the "historic" 90-minute meeting that President Donald Trump had with his Chinese and Russian counterparts. But official sources said India is following the summit and likely ramifications with strategic caution. The meeting ended with a declaration that committed to UN reforms, stable energy flows, nuclear risk reduction and the "abuse" of its jurisdiction by the International Criminal Court.

NEW DELHI: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah on Thursday said he would not contest the next Assembly election, citing his age and the physical difficulties associated with campaigning.Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, Siddaramaiah said he was now 80 years old and found it increasingly difficult to move around as he used to.“What can one say at this age? I am now 80 years old. That is why I have said I will not contest the next election,” he said.Siddaramaiah added that while his supporters continued to urge him to contest, he had decided against it because of his advancing age.He also rejected Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy's allegation that he was being sidelined within the Congress, maintaining that there was no such situation. The controversy arose after Siddaramaiah was seated in the fifth row at an event in Delhi to launch Congress parliamentary chairperson Sonia Gandhi's memoir. DK Shivakumar dismisses speculation of rift with SiddaramaiahMeanwhile, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday dismissed speculation of differences between him and Siddaramaiah, alleging that some people were attempting to create an impression of a rift between the two leaders.Speaking to reporters near Mekhri Circle and Town Hall, Shivakumar said Siddaramaiah remained their leader and that he had recently met him to discuss various issues, including the upcoming local body elections."There is no big rift or small rift between former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and me. Some people are trying to create an atmosphere that there is a rift between us," he said."In politics, there should be critics; there should be opponents. It is only when they are there that people like us can do clean politics. Siddaramaiah is our leader. Some people, including Mahaswamiji, are projecting it differently in the media. We have already conveyed to him whatever we had to convey regarding these matters," he added.Explaining the reason for his meeting with Siddaramaiah, Shivakumar said, "Local body elections are approaching. So I had to discuss many issues with him, and therefore I met him and exchanged festival greetings."Siddaramaiah had earlier ruled out contesting 2028 pollsSiddaramaiah had earlier announced that he would not contest the 2028 Karnataka Assembly elections , citing his advancing age and saying that politics had become "deeply polluted".However, the Congress Working Committee member had maintained that he would remain active in politics and continue to raise his voice on issues concerning people's hardships and well-being.Siddaramaiah resigned as chief minister on May 28 following directions from the Congress high command, paving the way for D K Shivakumar to take over as the state's chief minister.

Article Title: Pati, patni aur woh: How wife's affair suspicion led to Pune airline staffer's murder
Article Text:
The victim, Varsha Turkar, worked with a leading airline and was posted at Pune airport.

Pati, Patni aur woh?





NAGPUR: A suspected extramarital relationship has emerged as the alleged motive behind the murder of a 23-year-old airline employee who was stabbed to death in the forests of Gondia, with police arresting four people, including the wife of the victim’s friend, in connection with the case on Friday.The victim, Varsha Turkar, worked with a leading airline and was posted at Pune airport. She had travelled to her maternal home in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh with her two-and-a-half-year-old daughter to celebrate Diwali. On November 14, she left home to meet her old friend, Nitesh Aggarwal, 42, a prominent realtor, at Bondarani in Gondia district, around 40km away.Varsha and Nitesh, who had reportedly been friends for over a decade, had gone for an outing to a remote forest stretch near the Wainganga river, close to the Maharashtra-Madhya Pradesh border. However, the outing turned tragic when Varsha was stabbed to death by three masked assailants near a Shiva temple in the Bondarani forests, under Dawaniwada police limits. Nitesh was the sole eyewitness to the murder.Police said the murder was a contract killing worth Rs 13 lakh, allegedly planned by Nitesh’s wife, Mona Aggarwal, 41. She was reportedly disturbed by her husband’s alleged relationship with Varsha and feared that it could lead to a divorce.According to police, Mona enlisted the help of a neighbour to hire contract killers, who followed the couple into the forest on a motorcycle.Police examined CCTV footage from around 300 cameras covering the Bondarani forests and areas including Tiroda, Khairlanji, Varashivni and Gondia. Cellphone surveillance, call data records and vehicle movement data also helped investigators track the suspects.Technical analysis, intelligence inputs and CCTV footage led police to history-sheeter Imran Karim Sheikh, 26, of Sanjaynagar Muri in Gondia. He was taken into custody on November 19 and allegedly confessed that Mona had planned Varsha’s murder.According to police, Mona first approached her neighbour, Kunal Kumbhalkar, 31, an affluent businessman. Kunal then contacted alleged gangster Shahrukh Pathan and paid him Rs 13 lakh to arrange Varsha’s murder.Shahrukh allegedly assigned the contract to three local youths from Sanjaynagar Muri — Imran Sheikh, Naylan Sheikh and Krish Raut.The accused tracked Nitesh’s car, which was registered in Mona’s name, using its iConnect app ID and password. This gave them access to the vehicle’s live GPS location, Gondia SP Gorakh Bhamre said. The three assailants allegedly attacked Varsha when the car stopped near the temple.Following Imran’s alleged confession, police detained Mona and Kunal on Friday and handed them over to Dawaniwada police along with Imran. All three were arrested along with Shahrukh Pathan. Two other accused, Naylan and Krish, are absconding.
Article Summary: The victim, Varsha Turkar, worked with a leading airline and was posted at Pune airport. She had travelled to her maternal home in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh with her two-and-a-half-year-old daughter to celebrate Diwali. On November 14, she left home to meet her old friend, Nitesh Aggarwal, 42, a prominent realtor, at Bondarani in Gondia district.

Article Title: Trump pushes Iran war decision to 2027, says he will 'see what happens' after January 1
Article Text:
Trump has signalled a pause in fresh attack on Iran this year

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Thursday said that he will wait until after the beginning of 2027 before deciding on any fresh military action against Iran, signalling a pause in his plans for a possible renewed bombing campaign."I'm not rushing into any decision [on Iran]. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year," Trump told Axios in a brief phone interview on Thursday while returning to the US from China. In a separate interview with Reuters, he made a similar statement saying, "Well, I'll talk to you about it after the beginning of the year."Trump's remarks come amid continuing tensions with Tehran, with Washington weighing the possibility of renewed strikes alongside Israel even as it maintains a naval blockade and economic pressure campaign against Iran. The US president has alternated between threatening escalation and suggesting that hostilities could wind down. Last week, he described another major round of strikes as "quite unlikely", although Axios reported on Wednesday that he was still considering a joint operation with Israel.The reported options include strikes on suspected Iranian nuclear facilities, including the Pickaxe Mountain site, as well as bridges, power plants and Iranian military and civilian leaders.The White House has also sought assessments from the Pentagon and intelligence agencies on how Tehran could retaliate against different strike scenarios, particularly the risk of attacks on oil and gas infrastructure in Gulf countries.Meanwhile, in a win for Trump the US Senate rejected a Democratic resolution seeking to end the Iran war, with a 48-51 vote, as Republicans backed Trump's military campaign. The vote, the first on the conflict since Republicans suffered losses in the midterm elections, came despite growing public opposition to the war, with about six in 10 voters saying US military action against Iran was the wrong decision, according to an AP survey. Three Republicans voted in favour of the resolution, while Democratic Senator John Fetterman joined Republicans in opposing it.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has also been reportedly pressing Washington to resume military action. The head of Israel's Mossad, Roman Gofman, visited the US last week for talks with CIA Director John Ratcliffe and White House envoy Steve Witkoff. An Israeli source, cited by Reuters, said Gofman was sent by Netanyahu to advocate renewed strikes. The discussions also included Israeli claims about Iranian research into chemical weapons, which Tehran has rejected as an attempt to create a pretext for military action.Trump's shift in timeline follows the November 3 midterm elections, in which Republicans suffered major losses and Democrats are set to take control of Congress in January. Before the polls, Trump had repeatedly suggested that Iran would be more willing to negotiate after the elections. His administration has since maintained that the US blockade and sanctions are working. The Senate on Thursday again rejected a measure seeking to curb Trump's war powers.The financial cost of the conflict is also coming under scrutiny. A Pentagon official told the Senate Armed Services Committee on Thursday that the war had cost an estimated $48.3 billion as of November 13. The figure includes military operations and the replacement of equipment and munitions, but excludes damage to US military bases in West Asia.Lawmakers have pressed the Pentagon to provide a separate assessment of that damage, with an Associated Press analysis pointing to billions of dollars in losses from Iranian missile and drone attacks.Trump also played down a report that Iran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in Washington, saying he did not think people in the US capital should be alarmed. However, he claimed Iran was looking at chemical and biological weapons. Iran's foreign ministry has dismissed US allegations about such weapons programmes as intended to create fear and justify military action.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump says he will wait until after the beginning of 2027 before deciding on any fresh military action against Iran. Trump's remarks come amid continuing tensions with Tehran, with Washington weighing the possibility of renewed strikes alongside Israel. The US Senate rejected a Democratic resolution seeking to end the Iran war, with a 48-51 vote.

Article Title: Bombay high court stops further demolition of Dawood Ibrahim's building over Waqf appeal status
Article Text:
The Bombay high court has intervened to stop the demolition of Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana, which includes a historic prayer hall





MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Thursday halted the demolition of Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana at Bhendi Bazaar in south Mumbai, which houses a 150-year-old prayer hall, and directed all parties to maintain status quo till next Wednesday. The court will hear a petition challenging BMC's action to pull down the structure.By the time the court passed its order, the civic body had demolished 60-70% of the structure, where underworld don Dawood Ibrahim 's family once lived. Following the court's directions, the prayer hall, measuring 1,582 sq ft, a portion of the first floor above it and certain portions at the rear of the building were left untouched.A bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna pulled up the petitioners, questioning why earlier notices and a final order had not been brought to its attention. The two Mumbai residents contended that the demolition notice was a fresh one, allegedly issued to facilitate a developer's project.Senior counsel Anil Sakhare, appearing for the BMC, told the court that the first notice had been issued in 2018. The bench cautioned the petitioners against withholding information relevant to the case and warned them against attempting to mislead the court. "Don't try to mislead the court.Don't take the court for a ride. We do not appreciate this," the bench told the petitioner.BMC had scheduled the demolition for Nov 18 and 19. The petitioners claimed they were "persons interested and beneficiaries of the Waqf institution". They said a notice was pasted on Nov 17, directing the occupants to vacate the premises by Nov 18.The petition alleged that the notice violated the principles of natural justice and was contrary to Supreme Court orders in a civil appeal filed by the Waqf Board in 2023.The petitioners also cited orders of the state Waqf tribunal and said an appeal was pending against a 2025 order of the Maharashtra State Board of Waqf (MSBW). They alleged that BMC was now "incorrectly" referring to a masjid as a "prayer hall".The high court directed all parties to maintain status quo and ordered that no further action be taken. BMC's counsel sought 30 minutes to withdraw the civic body's manpower from the site on Thursday.The court posted the matter for further hearing on Wednesday and directed the BMC to file an affidavit.
Article Summary: Bombay high court halts demolition of Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana in south Mumbai. Court orders all parties to maintain status quo till next Wednesday. Court will hear a petition challenging BMC's action to pull down the structure.

Article Title: No invite for China at Anthropic IPO: After SpaceX, Claude parent too shuts Chinese investors out
Article Text:
Anthropic IPO

Why keep Chinese investors at arm's length?

Trump and Xi may be talking, but technology remains a sticking point

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!Earlier billionaire Elon Musk's AI and aerospace giant SpaceX barred investors from Hong Kong and mainland China from buying its shares. Now, Anthropic followed a similar route. While the IPO was open only to investors from selected countries, the repeated exclusion of Chinese investors by major US technology companies raises questions.The artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot reportedly turned away investment from Chinese and Hong Kong firms ahead of its public listing, in what went on to record as the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history.Three people familiar with the decision said Anthropic had excluded investors from the two regions, New York Times reported.The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. As Washington and Beijing compete for supremacy in AI, technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in their already strained relationship.The exclusion comes against the backdrop of a growing technology rivalry between the US and China.The Trump administration has been taking steps to restrict China's access to advanced AI technology, while both countries are drawing red lines around their homegrown technologies.Anthropic's decision appears in line with a wider trend among major American technology companies. SpaceX and its bankers had taken a similar step ahead of the company's blockbuster IPO in July, shutting Chinese investors out of the offering.OpenAI, another leading AI company, is also expected to bar Chinese investors from its eventual public listing. It has already prevented investors from China from participating in its private fund-raising rounds.There is another common thread connecting all three companies: Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI have all counted the US government among their clients.The decision also comes at an interesting moment in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on Thursday at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China, with both leaders looking to bring some stability and goodwill into an increasingly rocky economic relationship.During the meeting, Xi called on members to build an "open ecosystem" for technology. Yet, while the two leaders are attempting to improve ties, their governments continue to build barriers around trade, technology and capital.The latest developments around AI chips underline just how difficult that balancing act is. Hours before Trump arrived in Asia for meetings with regional leaders, his administration moved to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.Beijing was quick to warn that it could respond with countermeasures if Washington continued with the restrictions."If the US persists, China will take countermeasures," China warned.A spokesman for China's Ministry of Commerce also expressed strong opposition to the latest US measures on Thursday."China is deeply concerned about — and firmly opposes — a series of recent economic and trade restrictive measures taken by the US against China," the spokesman told NYT.The latest restrictions on artificial intelligence are adding to a series of escalating moves by both countries. China experts have warned that the new AI rule could make it harder for Trump and Xi to reach any meaningful agreement to ease tensions.
Article Summary: Anthropic turned away Chinese and Hong Kong investors ahead of its IPO. Elon Musk's SpaceX also barred Chinese investors from its IPO in July. The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. Technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in US-China relations.

PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'

Death sentence and legal proceedings
