NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: Lucknow Police’s operation narco hunt tracks Odisha ganja trail; two smugglers arrested with 48.8 kg haul
Article Text:
Lucknow Police apprehended two suspected smugglers and confiscated 48.80 kg of ganja during a recent operation

Crime Branch seeks public inputs to crack organised crime networks





LUCKNOW: Tracking an interstate narcotics trail from Odisha to Lucknow, the Crime Branch of Lucknow Police has arrested two alleged smugglers and seized 48.80 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth Rs 35 lakh, under its ongoing Operation Narco Hunt. The accused were allegedly transporting consignments of ganja from Odisha for supply in Lucknow and adjoining districts.The breakthrough came when the Crime Branch received intelligence that two men allegedly involved in bringing ganja from Odisha were waiting in a red car near the Municipal Corporation office on Bandha Road. Acting on the tip-off, a police team rushed to the spot, cordoned off the area and intercepted the vehicle, arresting both occupants.A search of the car led to the recovery of 43 packets containing 48.80 kg of ganja, two Android mobile phones and Rs 540 in cash. The red car, bearing registration number JH01CC9687, which was allegedly used to transport the contraband, was also seized. Police estimated the seized ganja to be worth Rs 35 lakh.The arrested accused have been identified as Prakash Dubey (49), a resident of Vishnu Puri Colony in Bamrauli, under Dhoomanganj police station in Prayagraj, and Jai Anand Mishra (45), a resident of Sector 3, Avadh Vihar Yojana, under Sushant Golf City police station in Lucknow.ADCP Kiran Yadav said that during preliminary interrogation, the accused disclosed that they used to procure ganja from Odisha and transport it to Lucknow for distribution in the city and adjoining districts."The Crime Branch has now launched an investigation into the interstate supply chain to identify the source of the contraband, the transportation route, intended buyers and other members allegedly involved in the racket. Investigators are attempting to trace the network beyond the two arrested men to identify those involved in procurement, interstate transportation and local distribution," ADCP Yadav said.An FIR has been registered at Aliganj police station under Case No. 227/2026, invoking Sections 8 and 20 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.The arrests are part of Operation Narco Hunt, launched by the Lucknow Police Commissionerate in accordance with the Union Ministry of Home Affairs' three-year Vision Document for 2026–2029 to intensify action against narcotics trafficking and organised drug networks.The campaign aims to dismantle drug supply chains by tracing the movement of narcotics from their source through transportation corridors to local distribution networks. Police are focusing on identifying organised syndicates, their operatives and the infrastructure used to transport drugs across state borders and supply them in local markets.As part of its intelligence-gathering mechanism against organised criminal networks, the Lucknow Crime Branch has also activated an organised crime helpline, 7839861034, and a technology-based Sutra Saarthi Bot. Police have appealed to citizens to share credible information about narcotics trafficking and organised crime through these channels, assuring them that the identities of informants would be kept confidential.The Crime Branch said intelligence inputs from the public could help track criminal networks, identify their operatives and facilitate targeted action against organised syndicates.
Article Summary: Lucknow Police seized 48.80 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth Rs 35 lakh. The accused were allegedly transporting consignments from Odisha to Lucknow. The arrests are part of Operation Narco Hunt, launched by the Lucknow Police Commissionerate.

Article Title: Gorakhpur bulldozer tragedy: Akhilesh Yadav accuses Yogi Adityanath of harassing PDA workers over boy's death
Article Text:
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav.

(With agency inputs)





LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Friday accused chief minister Yogi Adityanath of targeting and harassing PDA activists and their families following the death of a 14-year-old boy, who was allegedly crushed by a bulldozer after party roadshow in Gorakhpur.PDA, a political acronym coined by Akhilesh Yadav in 2023, refers to 'Pichhde' (backward classes), Dalits and 'Alpsankhyak' (minorities).In a detailed post on X, the SP chief alleged that CCTV footage had contradicted the chief minister's version of the incident and accused the state government of intimidating party workers."Now that CCTV footage has exposed the lies spread by the Uttar Pradesh chief minister about a child killed in an accident in Gorakhpur, he has become flustered."In desperation at the prospect of being disgraced worldwide, he is now harassing our PDA activists and their families," Yadav wrote.His remarks came a day after police arrested five people in connection with the boy's death, PTI reported.An SP leader, Sadhu Yadav, whose name figures in the FIR, was taken from his residence to the AIIMS-Gorakhpur police station for questioning. His family subsequently shared a video on social media, alleging that police personnel had surrounded their house.Responding to the alleged police action, Akhilesh urged party workers not to be intimidated and questioned the longevity of the present government's political authority."We will tell our brave activists not to fear this cruelty and injustice, because the chief minister is only a guest here for another two or three months. His power will not last much longer," he said.The former CM also alleged internal discord within the BJP's state leadership, claiming that the party's state president was threatening Adityanath over an alleged plan to establish a separate political outfit.He further claimed that the state organisation was pressuring the chief minister to sign a 'rejection letter' aimed at declaring the list of candidates prepared by him as "fake."Yadav also alleged that Adityanath lacked adequate support within his own party, claiming that even 10 BJP MLAs were not standing by him.Referring to the controversy surrounding alleged deletion of voters' names, the SP chief said the deputy chief minister, apparently referring to Keshav Prasad Maurya, had contradicted the claims. He also cited the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's clarification on the issue."The deputy chief minister (apparently hinting towards Keshav Prasad Maurya) in his own government has contradicted them, stating that no voter's name has been deleted. Even the chief electoral officer of Uttar Pradesh has dismissed their claims, clarifying that they do not provide any data based on religion," Yadav said on X.Turning his criticism towards the government's functioning, the SP chief alleged that various sections, including young people, shopkeepers and investors, were dissatisfied with the administration.He accused the government of widespread corruption and alleged that investors were being asked to pay a 5 per cent advance commission, while contractors were facing demands for a 50 per cent advance payment."Investors are troubled by the demand for a 5 per cent advance commission, while contractors are plagued by a 50 per cent advance demand. The public can see the consequences and evidence of rampant commission-seeking behaviour in every construction project --- be it collapsing highways and failing water tanks and bridges," he alleged.Yadav further claimed that the government's alleged conduct towards professors, journalists, bureaucrats and lawyers had alienated intellectuals.He also criticised the discontinuation of the 'Yash Bharati' award, claiming that the decision had distanced talented artists, creative professionals, doctors, engineers, chartered accountants and sportspersons from the government.Questioning the BJP government's claims on law and order, the SP president alleged that its narrative had been exposed by incidents of violence and administrative failures."How can someone who has openly shattered law and order, literally firing bullets to tear it apart, be considered to have good conduct? It is worth remembering that the chief minister even had criminal cases against himself withdrawn," he said.Yadav further questioned the government's ability to maintain law and order, saying the public was now questioning the administration's credibility."The public is now asking, "how can those for whom crime is a standard operating procedure ever improve law and order?"" he said.Predicting an electoral setback for the BJP, the SP chief asserted that the ruling party would lose the upcoming election because of what he described as a complete breakdown of law and order.He also alleged that the BJP leadership and its candidates were collectively working towards removing him from the political scene, PTI reported.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav accuses Yogi Adityanath of targeting and harassing PDA activists and their families. Yadav's remarks came a day after police arrested five people in connection with a 14-year-old boy's death. He also alleged internal discord within the BJP's state leadership.

Article Title: A federal judge rules Brooke Rollins' religious emails to roughly 100,000 USDA employees unconstitutional and restricts the use of her official account
Article Text:
US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins.

Judge says Rollins crossed boundaries with Christian messages

USDA considers appeal as religious messaging sparks debate

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A US federal judge has ordered Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to stop sending religious messages to employees through her official government email account, ruling that her communications crossed boundaries by assuming that staff members shared her Christian beliefs.US District Judge Trina Thompson issued the order on Thursday while granting a preliminary injunction sought by federal employees who accused Rollins of using her position to promote Christianity within the Department of Agriculture (USDA). The judge said the secretary must recognise limits when communicating religious messages and cannot use her official authority to pressure subordinates."The Court ORDERS that the Secretary must recognise certain boundaries when communicating religious messages," Thompson wrote in her ruling.The case was brought by seven USDA employees from different religious backgrounds, including those who do not identify with any religion. They alleged that Rollins had sent increasingly religious messages to the department's entire workforce, making employees feel excluded and pressured to conform to her beliefs.According to the complaint, Rollins began sending department-wide holiday emails shortly after taking office.Some of the messages included references to Jesus Christ, Christmas and the resurrection of Jesus.In a Christmas message sent on December 23, 2025, Rollins said that the spirit of generosity came from "the very first Christmas when God gave us the greatest gift possible, the gift of his Son and our Savior Jesus Christ".In another message sent on Easter, April 5, 2026, she described the occasion as "the greatest story ever told" and referred to employees as being like the first disciples who encountered the risen Christ.The employees argued that the messages amounted to government-sponsored religious promotion and violated the First Amendment's protections against the establishment of religion.Thompson agreed that the communications went too far, finding that they created pressure on employees to accept or appear to share the secretary's religious beliefs.The judge also took issue with Rollins' repeated use of words such as "we", "us" and "our" in the messages, saying the language suggested that employees universally shared her Christian beliefs. She noted that the emails did not acknowledge employees who followed other religions or held no religious beliefs.The court also rejected the argument that employees could simply ignore the messages, pointing out that Rollins used the same official email account to communicate important departmental information, including agency restructuring and government shutdown plans."Why should the secretary be exempt from her own rules? The buck stops with Secretary Rollins," Thompson wrote, adding that her senior position warranted greater scrutiny because she sat at the top of the agency's hierarchy.The judge clarified that the order did not prevent Rollins from expressing her faith in her personal capacity or discussing religion with colleagues who were interested.The USDA said it was evaluating all available options, including filing an appeal, and described the ruling as a "completely unprecedented attempt to muzzle a Cabinet Secretary".The department had argued that Rollins was merely sharing her personal views about religious holidays and was neither conducting religious exercises nor forcing employees to follow her beliefs.However, Thompson pointed to the department's own November 2025 guidance on religious expression in the workplace, saying Rollins should follow the boundaries outlined in her own directives. The guidance allows employees to discuss their faith with interested colleagues but prohibits persistent unwanted religious advances and the use of official authority to pressure subordinates.The ruling comes amid a wider debate over the role of religion in the Trump administration. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has incorporated Christian prayer into activities at the Pentagon, while critics have accused administration officials of blurring the separation between religion and government.Advocates of church-state separation have also raised concerns over religious messaging by senior officials and the use of government platforms to promote Christianity.The USDA ruling, however, does not prevent Rollins from practising or expressing her faith privately. It restricts the use of her official government communication channels in ways that could amount to religious coercion in the workplace.
Article Summary: Judge says Rollins cannot use her position to pressure employees into following her religious beliefs. The ruling is in response to complaints that the messages violated the First Amendment right to freedom of speech. The judge says the ruling does not prevent Rollins from expressing her faith in private.

Article Title: UK acts to secure thousands of commercial fridges after Europe cyberattacks
Article Text:
File photo: An employee works on empty freezers in a store where a cyberattack has taken down several of its freezers (Representative Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Britain has carried out a major cybersecurity operation to protect tens of thousands of commercial fridges and freezers from potential hacking. Recent attacks on refrigeration systems across Europe spoiled food worth millions of euros and disrupted supermarkets.The operation involved major supermarket chains, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums, with thousands of devices used to control refrigeration systems taken offline as a precaution. In some cases, staff were asked to physically disconnect internet cables and monitor temperatures manually, the BBC reported.The vulnerability was discovered in late October by ethical hackers at British firm Omega Systems, who examined the security of refrigeration controllers made by Resource Data Management (RDM). Experts at Pen Test Partners helped verify the weakness and alert authorities.The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs and the Food Standards Agency joined the effort to warn businesses and plug the security gaps. IT teams at major supermarket chains were diverted to the task, with one employee telling the BBC that hundreds of devices were taken offline each day over a week.The urgency followed a series of attacks on commercial refrigeration systems in Europe. In France, hundreds of supermarkets and food processing sites were hit in October after hackers targeted temperature-control systems made by Danish firm Danfoss. A further wave in early November affected stores across seven European countries, with Belgium and Luxembourg among the worst hit.French intelligence and cybersecurity agencies blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for the October attack, which reportedly affected around 700 commercial sites and triggered 15 fires after hackers raised temperatures in refrigeration systems. Tehran has denied the accusation.Security researchers warned that Britain's refrigeration controllers had weaknesses, including problems involving weak passwords. However, RDM disputed comparisons with the European attacks, saying exploiting its systems would have required physical access to specific hardware.RDM chief executive Ged Evans said the vulnerability was identified in a test environment and that the assessment involved dismantling the company's hardware. He said the company had already released initial software patches, contacted customers and recommended steps to reduce risks. RDM also said it had found no evidence of malicious activity on its controllers.The BBC said the operation had been kept under wraps to avoid alerting potential attackers before businesses could secure their systems.
Article Summary: Operation involved major supermarket chains, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums. Staff were asked to physically disconnect internet cables and monitor temperatures manually. Vulnerability discovered in late October by ethical hackers at British firm Omega Systems. Security researchers warned that Britain's refrigeration controllers had weaknesses.

Article Title: Collapses, illegal construction spark protests at MCD meet
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Incidents of building collapses and the alleged failure of Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to prevent illegal construction despite repeated complaints rocked its standing committee meeting Thursday, with AAP councillors questioning the effectiveness of the civic body’s action against erring officials.Rafia Mahir, AAP councillor from Bazar Sita Ram, alleged that several complaints lodged by her regarding illegal construction and dilapidated buildings in her ward fell on deaf ears. Many of the houses are old and can neither be easily reconstructed nor repaired, she added.“I approached the deputy commissioner and executive engineer and even provided specific addresses where illegal construction was taking place. But no action was taken. After the recent incident of a building collapse, the CM came for barely two minutes. We are behaving as if the people who died simply didn’t exist,” Mahir said.Protesting against what they termed as growing corruption in the building department, AAP councillors wore safety gear before entering the meeting room. Leader of opposition Ankush Narang claimed the councillors were forced to remove their helmets, their placards were snatched and they were prevented from recording videos during the meeting.“Buildings are collapsing across Delhi, costing innocent lives; yet, But BJP is not concerned with public safety,” he posted on X.Praveen Kumar, AAP councillor from Janakpuri, said Narela zone, with 16 wards, has only two junior engineers (JEs) and one assistant engineer (AE). Rohini zone, with 12 wards, has two AEs and one JE, while Najafgarh zone, covering 22 wards, has three AEs and three JEs. In City Sadar Paharganj zone, two AEs and two JEs are available for 12 wards. “Further, against the requirement of 18 divisions in the building department across 12 zones, there are only 13 executive engineers, leaving several divisions inadequately staffed,” he said.The councillors also flagged the deteriorating condition of community halls in the city, alleging that many of them were poorly maintained and lacked basic facilities, including safe drinking water. Standing committee chairperson Satya Sharma directed officials to conduct a survey of the halls within one week to identify dilapidated and unsafe buildings.The committee, meanwhile, cleared several pending proposals, including the development of Lahori Gate museum, road-cutting permissions under Dig and Restore Policy, discount in regularisation of built-up area under PM-UDAY scheme, development of Nigam Shri Schools of Excellence, draft Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 and transfer of operations of 13 sports stadiums under public-private partnership (PPP) model. Proposals related to CT scan and MRI facilities at MCD hospitals were also approved.
Article Summary: AAP councillors question effectiveness of the civic body’s action against erring officials. Councillors wore safety gear before entering the meeting room. Leader of opposition Ankush Narang claimed councillors were forced to remove their helmets, their placards were snatched and they were prevented from recording videos.

Article Title: 4-time Congress MLA and ex-Haryana minister Phool Chand Mullana passes away
Article Text:
He served multiple times as a cabinet minister while holding important portfolios in the government.





AMBALA: Senior Congress leader Phool Chand Mullana, who represented the Mullana assembly constituency in Ambala district four times, passed away on Friday.He served as a cabinet minister in the Haryana government and held several portfolios, including revenue, public works department (PWD), education, forest and technical education. He was awarded the Haryana Ratan in 2005 for his contribution to the state's politics and social welfare.His son, Ambala MP Varun Chaudhry, shared a social media post announcing his father's demise, saying, “Our leader and my father Chaudhry Phool Chand Mullana.”His daughter-in-law, Pooja Chaudhry, is the sitting MLA from Mullana.Ambala District Congress Committee (Urban) president Pawan Aggarwal said the party received news of Mullana's demise on Friday morning. Mullana had been unwell and was hospitalised due to age-related ailments.He had also stayed away from political activities for some time due to his health condition.MP Varun said his father's last procession would begin at 11am on Saturday, November 21, from their residence in Sector 7, Ambala City, and proceed to the cremation ground at Rambagh, Sector 7.
Article Summary: Phool Chand Mullana served as a cabinet minister in the Haryana government. He represented the Mullana assembly constituency in Ambala district four times. Mullana had been unwell and was hospitalised due to age-related ailments. He had also stayed away from political activities for some time due to his health.

Article Title: Bengaluru man kills 18-year-old stepson, attacks wife with knife and hammer over 'affair'
Article Text:
Sudeep was arrested for the alleged murder of his wife's teenage son amidst a violent quarrel in Padmanabhanagar





BENGALURU: A 44-year-old man allegedly attacked his wife and her 18-year-old son with a knife and hammer, killing the teenager and leaving the woman injured before locking her inside a room and fleeing following a domestic quarrel in Bengaluru, police said on Friday.The accused was arrested after the incident came to light nearly three days later.The accused, identified as Sudeep, who had previously worked in the private banking sector, allegedly attacked Seema (43) and her son Soham at their apartment in Padmanabhanagar, under Banashankari police station limits, on November 16, police said.Citing preliminary investigation, a senior police officer said Sudeep was Seema's second husband, while Soham was her son from her first marriage.The accused allegedly suspected Seema of having an illicit relationship, triggering a quarrel between them. Seema worked at an insurance company.According to police, the attack took place between 9 pm and 11 pm on November 16, after which Sudeep allegedly fled.The incident came to light following a complaint by B Mallayya, who had rented out his flat in Padmanabhanagar to Seema from October 3, 2024. She was living there with her husband and son.In his complaint, Mallayya said he had received complaints from neighbours over the past six months about frequent quarrels and arguments among the family members.He said he had repeatedly advised them to maintain peace and had also asked them to vacate the flat.On November 16, around 9 pm, the flat owner received calls from neighbours but was at work. About an hour later, he contacted the security guard, who told him there was no disturbance at the flat at that time, the senior police officer said.On the night of November 19, when Mallayya visited the flat, nobody responded from inside. He then went to Banashankari police station along with his friends and alerted the police.Subsequently, Mallayya, police personnel and Seema's friends went to the flat and found it locked. A locksmith was called to open the doors around 11 pm.On entering, they noticed bloodstains on the floor and walls. They then heard Seema screaming from a locked room inside the house, which was opened with the locksmith's help, the officer said.During questioning, Seema told police that Sudeep had quarrelled with her and Soham between 9 pm and 11 pm on November 16 before attacking them.Soham died in the assault, while Sudeep allegedly attempted to kill her as well. Seema sustained injuries but managed to lock herself inside a room.Police found Soham's body in the bathroom.Based on Seema's complaint, police registered a case against Sudeep under sections 103(1) (murder) and 109(1) (attempt to murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. He was subsequently arrested, police added.
Article Summary: The accused, identified as Sudeep, allegedly attacked Seema (43) and her son Soham at their apartment in Padmanabhanagar, under Banashankari police station limits, on November 16. The incident came to light following a complaint by B Mallayya, who had rented out his flat to Seema.

Article Title: Versova locals protest felling of 89 trees at park
Article Text: Mumbai: Several angry residents as well as citizen activists gathered at Versova's Nana Nani park in on Thursday, a day after BMC began the process of the felling of mature trees for the construction of a bridge as a part of the Mumbai coastal road-north. Some even held placards in their hands with messages like 'We need trees to exist - Save Nana Nani Park, Swachh Mumbai, Harit (green) Mumbai?'The tree removal is being carried out in phases. In the first phase, the civic body cut down 44 trees on Wednesday, while 28 others are proposed to be transplanted. In total, 89 trees are slated to be cut, while another 48 are proposed to be transplanted.Film actor Bhumika Chawla, who has worked in Hindi films like Tere Naam with Salman Khan, was also seen at the protest site with a placard in her hand opposing the axing. In a social media post on Instagram, she wrote, "26 years of Nana Nani Park in Versova and the trees are being cut for Development and Connection. Green shade, taken away - we are developing the infrastructure but aren't going to be left in the next few years with pure air - the Place to walk will maybe be malls. When are we going to stop this or find an alternative to green cover going and a CONCRETE Jungle coming to replace it."There was heavy police presence including that of women around the felling site, with some residents even being taken to the police station. Actor Pooja Ruparel, known for playing 'Chutki' in the film DDLJ, broke down while recording workers cutting a banyan tree at the park. In a post on Instagram, she was taken to the police station by the local police at the site and said that this is her first trip to the police station for doing the right thing.Meanwhile, Clyde Crasto, National Spokesperson, NCP-SP, said, "When coastal road south was being built, they did the same to South Mumbai's Tata Garden at Breach Candy with the promise of replanting the trees but the garden is like a graveyard today.BMC led by the BJP does not care for Mumbikars. First they pose for photos at the environmental Earthshot prize function with celebrities and then kill the environment by cutting our green lungs."Citizen activist Dhaval Shah, who was also at the site, said, "There were around 15-20 people protesting when I reached the site at around 11.30 am which was just a spontaneous gathering of many angry people. We believe this could have been avoided with better planning and the use of modern technology," said Shah.Many actors like Richa Chadha and Dia Mirza also came out in support of the park on social media, posting videos of the tree cutting. Local BJP MLA Ameet Satam said, "We will ensure that the garden is restored once the bridge construction work is complete. The permission for this tree cutting was taken as this was a DP road on which the green space had come up on the condition that the land would be given up whenever need arises. "
Article Summary: The tree removal is being carried out in phases. In the first phase, the civic body cut down 44 trees on Wednesday, while 28 others are proposed to be transplanted. Actor Pooja Ruparel, known for playing 'Chutki' in the film DDLJ, broke down while recording workers cutting a banyan tree at the park.

Article Title: Maharashtra govt's announcement to rename Dadar railway station turns out to be a faux pas, CMO clarifies a day later that only Dadar Metro station will be renamed
Article Text:
On Wednesday, the state government announced the renaming of Dadar railway station to Chaityabhoomi, which later was clarified.





MUMBAI: The state govt's announcement on Wednesday that Dadar railway station would be renamed Chaityabhoomi turned out to be a faux pas, with the chief minister's office (CMO) clarifying a day later that it was Dadar Metro station, and not the railway station, that would be renamed.The CMO pointed to the Director General of Information and Public Relations (DGIPR) for the error. Sources said the press release issued by the department had caused embarrassment to the govt.Wednesday's DGIPR release was headlined: "Dadar railway station to be named Chaityabhoomi. The legislature will fulfil the necessary requirements during the session - CM Devendra Fadnavis." It also stated that the govt had sent a letter to the Centre conveying in-principle approval to the demand for renaming Dadar railway station. Quoting Fadnavis, the release said the Centre had subsequently issued guidelines requiring a legislative committee for the process and that the necessary formalities would be completed during the legislative session.The release was also posted on Fadnavis's X handle. On Thursday morning, the CMO reissued the same release, replacing references to Dadar railway station with Dadar Metro station.Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad welcomed the decision to rename Dadar Metro station but said this was akin to naming a junction."A metro station is very local and there is a metro station every 500 metres. Also, we strongly object to first putting the name of a corporate and then the name of the metro station. We see this on all metro routes. For the govt, naming a station is a commercial sentiment, not an emotional one. Dadar Metro station is today called SBI-Dadar. When it is renamed Chaityabhoomi, there should be no corporate prefix," she said.Gaikwad said her party's demand to rename Dadar railway station remained unchanged.Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Arvind Sawant said BJP had promised to rename several south Mumbai railway stations before the assembly polls but was yet to do so. "Dr Ambedkar is too big a personality to be commemorated through a mere Metro station."Wednesday's announcement triggered a flurry of reactions on social media. Virag Dhulia posted a tongue-in-cheek message imagining a local train announcement in which Chaityabhoomi featured among its stops, prompting a confused passenger to ask whether the train would not go to Dadar.Krishnaraj Acharya questioned whether the renaming would reduce peak-hour crowds or improve passenger facilities. Reacting to the govt's clarification that it was Dadar Metro station, and not the railway station, that would be renamed, Acharya posted: "Good sense prevails."
Article Summary: State govt's announcement on Wednesday that Dadar railway station would be renamed Chaityabhoomi turned out to be a faux pas. The chief minister's office (CMO) clarified a day later that it was Dadar Metro station, and not the railway station, that would be rename.

Article Title: Mumbai woman constable bursts firecrackers inside Andheri police station to celebrate senior inspector's transfer, claims she will get 6 more officers shifted
Article Text:
(AI image) A woman constable at Andheri police station celebrated the transfer of Senior Inspector Umesh Machindar.





MUMBAI: A woman constable attached to Andheri police station allegedly burst firecrackers on the station premises on Tuesday to celebrate the transfer of senior inspector Umesh Machindar to Mumbai Police's Special Branch-I. Police personnel who witnessed the incident said the act was captured on the station's CCTV cameras.The constable had allegedly threatened Machindar with further action and claimed she would get six more police officers transferred from Andheri police station. Officers at the station said nobody dared to confront her.One officer alleged the constable frequently avoided official and security duties, threatened to die by suicide when assigned work and intimidated colleagues by claiming her husband was an IPS officer.The transfer order, based on the minutes of a Police Establishment Board meeting held on Nov 13, cited public interest, law and order, and administrative exigencies as reasons for the move. It directed the assistant commissioner of police or senior police inspector concerned to relieve Machindar immediately and submit a compliance report.The reason for the sudden transfer was not officially disclosed. However, police personnel alleged that it followed a complaint filed by the constable with senior authorities and was ordered without a departmental inquiry."I have been targeted by the woman constable. She had warned me that I would face action for assigning her duties. I was transferred based on her complaint, and no departmental inquiry was initiated to hear my side," Machindar said on Thursday.
Article Summary: A woman constable at Andheri police station celebrated the transfer of Senior Inspector Umesh Machindar. Police personnel who witnessed the incident said the act was captured on the station's CCTV cameras. One officer alleged the constable frequently avoided official and security duties.

Article Title: Dharavi locals boycott 2-day awareness campaign in Mumbai
Article Text:
Dharavi





Mumbai: A majority of residents of Shahu Nagar BMC buildings in the Dharavi Notified Area boycotted the two-day awareness camp organised by the Dharavi Redevelopment Project/Slum Rehabilitation Authority along with Adani Navbharat Developers Pvt Ltd on Nov 18 and 19.There are around 876 tenants residing in these buildings and a majority have opposed the redevelopment project for its lack of clarity and transparency. A resident, on condition of anonymity, said the buildings are spread over 13 acres but as per the proposed redevelopment plan the rehabilitation towers for the tenants will come up on only 1.5 acres.Authorities have urged the tenants to execute the tripartite agreement within the next 30 days. A press release stated permanent rehabilitation homes will be provided in the same locality within five years from the handover of the redevelopment site.
Article Summary: A majority of residents of Shahu Nagar BMC buildings in the Dharavi Notified Area boycotted the two-day awareness camp. There are around 876 tenants residing in these buildings and a majority have opposed the redevelopment project for its lack of clarity and transparency.

Article Title: Torres money laundering case: Ukrainian in ED custody till tomorrow
Article Text:
Money laundering





Mumbai: Extradited from Romania on Tuesday, Ukrainian citizen Oleksandr Zapichenko, also known as Alex, was allegedly involved in collecting about Rs 500 crore in cash from Torres Jewellery showrooms, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) told a special court on Thursday while seeking his custodial interrogation in the Platinum Hern-run Torres Jewellery outlet money laundering case. Zapichenko (38), a key accused in the case, was remanded to ED custody till Saturday after the agency said it needed to trace cryptocurrency transfers and alleged offshore beneficiaries.While the fraud has so far been pegged at Rs 177 crore, the ED submitted during Thursday’s remand hearing that the cash allegedly collected by Zapichenko was used to acquire USDT and was later liquidated outside India. “On the basis of the analysis of the material in possession, there are reasons to believe that… Zapichenko has directly indulged and been involved in the process or activity connected with the proceeds of crime including its concealment, possession, acquisition or use and projecting it as untainted,” the ED submitted. The agency said this showed the need for custodial questioning, especially as Zapichenko is a foreign national.Special public prosecutor Sunil Gonsalves, appearing for the ED, submitted that Zapichenko had been associated with the organisation since its inception and had arranged funds through cryptocurrency. Gonsalves said the cryptocurrency was converted into cash through Alpesh Khara and Lallan Singh, and that the funds were allegedly laundered and shown as legitimate money.Zapichenko’s defence lawyers Prashant Pandey and Pranay Saraf opposed the remand and questioned the legality of the arrest.According to the remand plea, Zapichenko was actively involved in cash collection, delivery of cash to Alpesh Khara or associates, and conversion of cash into USDT cryptocurrency. The ED claimed that several witnesses, including company personnel, auditors, cashiers and vendors, identified Zapichenko as a key management figure associated with Platinum Hern and its operations.The application also described a coded cash-distribution system allegedly used by Torres staff. The ED said a senior cashier at the Dadar showroom identified Zapichenko from a photograph and stated that Alex or “Mr A” in the Telegram group gave instructions for cash disbursement. The agency said another cashier claimed that cash of around Rs 2 crore to Rs 3 crore per day, and about Rs 120 crore to Rs 150 crore in two months, was handed over under instructions from management, including Zapichenko.On the USDT transfers, the defence said the agency had nothing beyond chats with “A”, who could have been anyone. The defence argued that in all these months, the ED could have identified who “A” was. It was also submitted that the alleged offence had already been investigated and that, apart from statements of co-accused, there was no material against Zapichenko.
Article Summary: Ukrainian citizen Oleksandr Zapichenko, also known as Alex, was allegedly involved in collecting about Rs 500 crore in cash from Torres Jewellery showrooms. He was remanded to ED custody till Saturday after the agency said it needed to trace cryptocurrency transfers and alleged offshore beneficiaries. The fraud has so far been pegged at Rs 177 crore.

A 40-year-old farmer was arrested on Wednesday for allegedly killing his two sons, , aged five and seven, by throwing them into Jayakwadi canal on Monday evening following frequent domestic disputes. The body of the elder son has been recovered from the canal.According to Pachod police in rural Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, accused Somnath alias Parameshwar Rodge (40) took his sons on the scooter on Monday evening on the pretext of buying chocolates, vada pav and taking them for an outing. “He allegedly threw both of them into the canal. Farmers who witnessed the incident tried to intervene, but he allegedly abused them and pelted stones at them,” police said.Pachod police registered a murder FIR against Rodge based on a complaint filed by his wife, Sushma (27) on Wednesday. “A group of farmers spotted Aryan alias Ayush Somnath Rodge around 9am in the Indegaon-Bramhagaon stretch of the canal while heading to switch on water pumps. They pulled the body out and alerted authorities. After a postmortem at the rural hospital in Pachod, the body was handed over to the family,” an officer said.Police said teams from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation fire department, divers and police personnel continued the search operation for five-year-old Shyam.Sub-divisional police officer Sunil Patil said Rodge told investigators that frequent arguments with his wife, Sushma (27), over their children’s upbringing had prompted the crime. “He has confessed that he wanted to kill both the children,” Patil said.Inspector Mahadev Naikwade of Pachod police said the accused also told investigators that he had planned to end his own life and had contemplated killing his wife too, but she had not accompanied him and therefore escaped “a similar fate” as their sons.Ayush’s last rites were performed at Nandar village on Wednesday evening amid tight police security. Police continue to investigate the circumstances leading to the crime.
Article Summary: A 40-year-old farmer was arrested on Wednesday for allegedly killing his two sons, aged five and seven, by throwing them into Jayakwadi canal on Monday evening. The body of the elder son has been recovered from the canal. Pachod police registered a murder FIR against the accused based on a complaint filed by his wife.

A man accused of murdering his wife on Monday allegedly died by suicide by jumping into a fire he set on his farm in Beed district late on Tuesday night. As Vishnu had gone missing and was reportedly the last person seen with his wife, he emerged as the prime suspect. A search operation was launched, but he remained untraceable.While the manhunt was under way, Vishnu allegedly took the extreme step around 9.30pm on Tuesday. “He set a heap of cotton stalks ablaze on his farmland in Anandwadi shivar and jumped into the flames, dying on the spot,” police said.Some villagers suspected that he might have been set on fire. Police, however, said preliminary findings pointed to suicide. Further investigations are under way.

Article Title: CJP conducts Lok Sabha seat-wise outreach programme across Maharashtra, focuses on youth mobilisation
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Cockroach Janta Party has launched a statewide organisational expansion drive across Maharashtra , stepping up Lok Sabha-level outreach to strengthen its grassroots network, recruit young volunteers, and build campaigns around local public issues such as education, employment, and civic accountability.As part of the four-day exercise led by national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde, party teams toured Satara, Kolhapur, Sangli and Solapur between Nov 14 and 17, holding meetings with youngsters, volunteers and local workers to expand the organisation at the constituency level.The Maharashtra campaign forms part of CJP’s nationwide expansion programme being coordinated by its national working committee through zonal committees across the country.According to a party statement issued on Wednesday, the delegation included West Zone in-charge Kshitij Pagar, joint organisation secretary Akshay Shinde, West Zone coordinator Sarosh Shaikh and local coordinators.During the tour, the party convened Lok Sabha-level volunteers’ meetings and outreach sessions in rural areas to gather feedback on local concerns and improve coordination among grassroots workers.“We will build a strong CJP team across Maharashtra that effectively raises the issues of the people. Building a strong organisational force to address the fundamental issues faced by the youth is the need of the hour. I am confident that the newly appointed team will effectively voice public concerns and spearhead the party’s expansion across the state,” Shinde said.The delegation also visited the homes of volunteers who had participated in party protests in Mumbai and Delhi, interacting with them and their parents to explain the party’s vision of building a transparent and accountable democratic movement driven by ordinary citizens.CJP simultaneously launched a membership drive, urging supporters to join Lok Sabha-level teams and participate in civic initiatives. It also began activities under its ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign aimed at highlighting and addressing issues in govt schools.CJP said its expansion strategy centres on establishing active representation from village to Lok Sabha levels, taking up public issues through ground-level interventions and developing young citizens as future leaders of the political movement.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party has launched a statewide organisational expansion drive across Maharashtra. Party teams toured Satara, Kolhapur, Sangli and Solapur between Nov 14 and 17. The Maharashtra campaign forms part of CJP’s nationwide expansion programme.

Article Title: 16-hour firefight brings Harsul waste plant blaze under control
Article Text:
Fire fighters dousing the flames at the Harsul waste processing unit

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

Two machines were damaged and a 15,000sqft dry waste shed was destroyed after a major fire broke out at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) waste processing unit in Harsul in the early hours of Wednesday.No casualties were reported in the incident, the authorities said. The fire brigade received a call around 4.35 am and dispatched five water tenders, along with several other tankers, to the site.Firefighters brought the blaze and internal combustion under control after nearly 16 hours, with a couple of water tenders kept on standby until night. According to local residents, thick smoke had engulfed the waste processing unit shortly after midnight.Municipal commissioner Amol Yedge, who visited the site, said waste processing had slowed down due to Diwali vacations , leading to a large accumulation of solid waste at the unit. “The heaps of waste helped the fire spread and turned it into a major one, making firefighting difficult,” he said.Yedge said an inquiry had been ordered into the fire incident. CCTV footage from the facility will be examined as part of the inquiry to ascertain how the fire started and whether there was any lapse.While the pre-sorting and baling machines and the shed suffered damage in the fire, Yedge said both the damaged machines were insured, and insurance claims will be made.Chief fire officer Ashok Khandekar said some of the metal sheets of the shed were broken to effectively facilitate firefighting.“Flames were flickering deep inside the smoldering waste heap, while dense white and grey smoke filled the structure and spread across the surrounding locality. Even if the fire was brought under control after 16 hours, we have kept two water tenders on standby to rule out further flare due to possible internal combustion of waste,” he said.The Harsul plant is one of the three main waste processing plants of the CSMC, along with Chikalthana and Padegaon. The fire incident is most likely to adversely impact the daily waste processing in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to a certain extent.
Article Summary: Two machines were damaged and a 15,000sqft dry waste shed was destroyed. The fire broke out at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) waste processing unit in Harsul. No casualties were reported in the incident.

Article Title: After YCMOU scam, section of stakeholders demand return to old offline evaluation
Article Text:
YCMOU

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

Several teachers, authorised examiners and student representatives have demanded that YCMOU scraps online paper checking and revert to old offline practice, following the irregularities flagged during answer sheet evaluation between June 9 and July 4 this year.About 19,231 answer sheets were allegedly evaluated by unauthorised people who misused biometric thumb impressions of authorised examiners at a college in Lasur Station Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. Complainants said the case has exposed the weakness of the online system.The demand has gained ground after Shillegaon police charged 48 people, including a college principal and a CAP centre director on Nov 15 for allegedly claiming Rs2,76,418 as remuneration for the unauthorised evaluation. While the irregularity occurred months ago at the CAP center, YCMOU authorities lodged an FIR only after its internal probes were over.“In the old practice, the examiner had to be physically present at the centre, take delivery of the answer sheet bundle, evaluate them in front of supervisors and return them after signing. There was no way to create a proxy in the examiner’s name,” said a teacher.In the online system, educational activist Tukaram Saraf said, the entire security rests on a biometric login.“Once the thumb impression is captured, the portal opens and anyone can sit on the terminal and evaluate. The physical absence of the authorised examiner becomes impossible to detect any wrongdoing,” he said.Stakeholders also argued that moderation was more effective in the offline system because moderators could see the marks given on answer sheets, the total count and remarks, if any, on papers. In online evaluation, they claimed, work is often hurried to meet targets, and errors go unnoticed till revaluation.“Technology that can be bypassed by a single thumb impression cannot be trusted with lakhs of answer sheets. A foolproof system with live CCTV monitoring, real-time physical verification of examiners and strict login audit is the need of the hour and YCMOU should return to the old practice of physical evaluation at CAP centres,” said Rahul Makasare, a student representative.When contacted, YCMOU spokesperson, Mahendra Bansode said no formal representation has been made so far demanding return to old offline evaluation.
Article Summary: About 19,231 answer sheets were allegedly evaluated by unauthorised people who misused biometric thumb impressions of authorised examiners at a college in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. Complainants said the case has exposed the weakness of the online system.

Article Title: CPR hosp tops govt medical colleges in state with 11 successful TAVI procedures
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:

TOI





The cardiology department of Chhatrapati Pramilaraje (CPR) govt hospital in Kolhapur has achieved the top position among Govt Medical Colleges (GMCs) across the state by successfully performing 11 Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) procedures.Recently, the department performed successful TAVI procedures on two patients on the same day — an 86-year-old man from Jaysingpur and a 77-year-old woman from Kolhapur. Both were considered high-risk for conventional open-heart surgery. According to Dean Sadanand Bhise, the patients recovered well, began walking the following day, and were discharged on the third day.Officials said both patients had severe calcification of the aortic valve, along with breathlessness, chest pain, dizziness and swelling in the legs. They also suffered from high blood pressure and diabetes. Considering their advanced age and the risks associated with open-heart surgery, the team, led by head of cardiology Akshay Bafna, performed the procedures using the TAVI technique.During the procedures, new heart valves measuring 29 mm and 26 mm were implanted through the femoral artery in the respective patients without opening their chests. Their quick recovery highlighted the department’s expertise in providing advanced cardiac treatment to critically ill patients.Bhise, while talking to, said, “Cardiology department performs around 150 to 200 advanced cardiac procedures every month. These include complex angioplasty, TAVI, pacemaker implantation, device closure, and neurovascular and peripheral vascular interventions. The department provides specialised treatment and is the only institution in western Maharashtra offering the DM Cardiology super-speciality course.”
Article Summary: The cardiology department of Chhatrapati Pramilaraje (CPR) govt hospital in Kolhapur has achieved the top position among Govt Medical Colleges (GMCs) across the state. It has successfully performed 11 Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) procedures.

Article Title: Eknath Shinde's helicopter fails to take off from Pandharpur due to battery issue; Maharashtra DyCM travels by road to Pune
Article Text:
Eknath Shinde’s helicopter encountered a technical issue with its battery before departing from Pandharpur (Photo credit: X)





PANDHARPUR: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde ’s helicopter developed a technical issue linked to its battery before taking off from Pandharpur in Solapur district on Thursday, forcing him to cancel his planned journey to Mumbai, a senior police official said.Solapur district superintendent of police (SP) Atul Kulkarni said the helicopter’s battery had discharged after it was started well ahead of its scheduled departure for Mumbai, news agency PTI reported.“The helicopter’s battery had discharged. Although the aircraft has two engines, only one started. The pilot had started the helicopter early as the departure was scheduled for 3pm. However, the departure was delayed by half an hour. As the battery was discharged, the issue prevented the chopper from taking off,” Kulkarni told PTI.Shinde, who was in the temple town of Pandharpur to review preparations for Kartiki Ekadashi, subsequently travelled by road to Pune airport, the officer said.“The helicopter did not take off at all. Therefore, travelling by road was the only option,” the SP added.Shinde is scheduled to attend the Kartiki Ekadashi Puja at the Lord Vitthal Temple in Pandharpur on November 21.Kartiki Ekadashi symbolises the end of Lord Vishnu’s four-month-long cosmic rest, known as chaturmasya.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: M Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde’s helicopter developed a technical issue linked to its battery before taking off from Pandharpur in Solapur district on Thursday. The helicopter's battery had discharged after it was started well ahead of its scheduled departure for Mumbai. The aircraft has two engines, only one started.
